title: Week 2 Mastery Quiz

questions.question: Which definition best matches “natural law”?
options: A tradition holding that moral principles can be discovered through reason and apply beyond enacted rules.
The people and interests represented by an elected official.
The administrative process of turning an adopted policy into operations and outcomes.
A system limiting total emissions and allowing permits to be traded.
questions.explanation: Natural law means a tradition holding that moral principles can be discovered through reason and apply beyond enacted rules.
choices: A tradition holding that moral principles can be discovered through reason and apply beyond enacted rules.
The people and interests represented by an elected official.
The administrative process of turning an adopted policy into operations and outcomes.
A system limiting total emissions and allowing permits to be traded.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “natural rights”?
options: Rights understood as inherent to persons rather than granted at a ruler’s discretion.
Strategic communication designed to mobilize belief or action, often through selective evidence and emotional technique.
Knowledge and skills needed to understand institutions, rights, responsibilities, and public decisions.
A public guarantee protecting eligible deposits up to legal limits.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “social contract”?

A testable claim about what is, was, or is likely to occur.

Legal authority to spend public money for a designated purpose.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “popular sovereignty”?
options: Produced tools, equipment, structures, and technology used to create other goods and services.
The principle that legitimate political authority depends on the people’s authorization.
The principle that political authority originates with the people.
A model with many firms, identical products, easy entry, and price-taking behavior.

The power to determine whether government action is consistent with the Constitution.
Formal approval of a constitution, treaty, or amendment.
Government through representatives and civic institutions oriented toward the public good.

Law developed through judicial decisions, custom, and precedent.
